Name: Shaylee Rademacher
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

I used the two slides from the slide deck that had a graph and an infographic. One was a graph about TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook, to name a few. The other was about Why Teens Drink Caffeine? I used these because I've been presenting graphs to help students learn to interpret graphs. Today I gave the 2 slides to my students, had them choose one of the slides, and had them use the They Say / I Say strategy. I did this as a Science Starter. It is low stakes and hopefully high engagement.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

I would like to use the They Say / I Say framework when students read their short articles from Science World. I will copy it onto paper so that students have the opportunity to interact with the article. This is just dipping my toe in the water with this strategy.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:

How would you use this strategy in the Science classroom, Julie? I would like to try this with a full article, not necessarily from the Science World magazine. I might need help finding the "just right" article about Space discovery that wouldn't be written on the astrophysicist level, but on a 7th-grade level.
